title: Introduction
text: Docs Get started Introduction Introduction Shadwire brings shadcn/ui's Open Code model to Ruby on Rails. The components are source code your application copies and then owns, with no runtime gem. shadcn/ui inverted how you relate to a UI library. Instead of installing a package and configuring what it allows from the outside, you copy the component's source into your project. Shadwire does the same for Rails. The components are ViewComponent classes styled with Tailwind CSS v4, distributed through a static registry and installed by a CLI. None of this becomes a runtime dependency The shadwire gem lives in the development group and exists only to install and sync files. Remove it and the installed components keep working exactly as they are. How it works The registry publishes, the CLI installs, and your app keeps the files. 1 The registry publishes Each component is published as a JSON document with its file contents inlined, served from https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r. Static files — no application server, no authentication. 2 The CLI installs bin/shadwire add button fetches the item, writes the files to their paths in your app, applies the gems and importmap pins it needs, and records all of it in shadwire.json. 3 You own it The files are yours. Edit variants, swap classes, rename things. bin/shadwire diff shows what has diverged from the registry. Copygem install shadwire shadwire init # shadwire.json + base files + bin/shadwire bin/shadwire add button card # installs components and their dependencies Principles Open Code The component's code is visible and editable in your repository. There is no configuration layer to work around: when the library did not anticipate your case, you change the file. Composition Subcomponents are nested helpers, not props: ui_card_header inside ui_card, ui_select_item inside ui_select_content. The view's structure mirrors the HTML's. Semantic tokens Every colour comes from a shadcn token (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground). Retheming means editing two lists of CSS variables; no component has to change. Accessible by default ARIA semantics and the WAI-ARIA APG patterns are built in: focus, keyboard, labels and states. The repository's suite checks it on every change. Ready for agents An agent skill and the llms.txt files describe the catalog in plain text, and the whole CLI speaks --json, so an agent reads the API instead of guessing at it. Explicit updates Nothing changes on its own. diff shows the divergence and update reapplies the registry's version when you say so, reporting what it overwrote. What is here already 57 components and 1 block, every one of them validated in the Rails application that serves this site. Area Components Forms field · input · textarea · checkbox · radio-group · switch · select · combobox · slider · input-otp · date-picker Overlays dialog · alert-dialog · sheet · drawer · popover · tooltip · hover-card Navigation sidebar · navigation-menu · menubar · breadcrumb · tabs · pagination · command Data table · data-table · chart · card · item · badge · avatar State skeleton · spinner · progress · empty · alert · sonner The whole catalog is under Components, and the CLI answers bin/shadwire list with the same list. Where to start Installation Requirements, the CLI, and your first component in your app. CLI Every command, every flag, and the JSON payload. Theming The tokens, your brand colour, and how to keep your edits. Agent skill The context Claude Code, Codex and other agents work from. Licence Shadwire is MIT, and the components the CLI installs into your app are yours: use them, modify them and ship them in commercial and closed-source products, with no attribution required in the installed files and no runtime dependency. Shadwire is a port of shadcn/ui, which is MIT as well. That notice, and the licences of everything an installed component brings with it (view_component, lucide-rails, the Lucide icons, Chart.js), are in the repository's NOTICE. Next Installation

title: Installation
text: Docs Get started Installation Installation Install the CLI, run init once, and start adding components. Requirements The installed components depend only on what your application already has. The registry declares these support floors: Requirement Version Why ruby >= 3.2 The syntax the components and the CLI use. rails >= 7.1 View helpers, the tag builder and the asset pipeline. view_component >= 4.0 The components are ViewComponent classes. lucide-rails >= 0.7 The Rails port of Lucide, shadcn/ui's icon set. Tailwind CSS v4 The tokens use @theme inline, which is v4. Interactive components need Stimulus 29 of the 57 components ship a Stimulus controller. They install into app/javascript/controllers/ and register themselves through importmap-rails' default eagerLoadControllersFrom. If your app registers controllers by hand, register the new ones too. bin/shadwire status --json reports what it found under stack. Install the CLI The CLI is a development-time tool and never becomes a runtime dependency. Install it globally or straight into the app — both work. Copy# global gem install shadwire # or straight into the app, in the development group bundle add shadwire --group development Run init From the root of the Rails app. It is the one command you run unprefixed, because it is the one that creates the binstub the others use. Copyshadwire init # gem installed globally bundle exec shadwire init # gem in the Gemfile What it does: shadwire.json: writes the manifest at the app root: registry, target aliases, the Tailwind entrypoint, and what is installed. Base files: installs app/components/ui_component.rb (the shared superclass) and vendor/shadwire/shadwire.css (the tokens). Base gems: adds view_component and lucide-rails to the Gemfile if they are missing. development group: adds shadwire itself to the Gemfile's development group. bin/shadwire: writes the binstub, the canonical entry point, resolved through the app's bundle. Tailwind @import: inserts the shadwire.css import into the Tailwind entrypoint. The command is idempotent: running it again undoes nothing, and an existing binstub is left alone. --force resets shadwire.json and rewrites the binstub. Why bin/shadwire After init, run everything through bin/shadwire. The binstub resolves through the app's bundle, so anyone who installs the development group runs the same version of the CLI, regardless of what each person happens to have installed globally. A bundle without the development group has no CLI bundle install --without development (common in deploys and in some CI jobs) does not install shadwire, and bin/shadwire will not run there. Install the development group in any job that uses the CLI, such as a drift check. Add your first component Copybin/shadwire add button Registry dependencies come along automatically. Each component installs its own helper module (button writes app/helpers/ui/button_helper.rb), and Rails includes everything under app/helpers/ in your views with no include. Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :outline, size: :sm) { "Save" } %> <%= render Ui::ButtonComponent.new(variant: :outline, size: :sm) do %> Save <% end %> The two forms are equivalent; prefer the helper in views. Confirm it worked Copybin/shadwire status status never fails. Outside a Rails app it answers "rails": false, an unreachable registry becomes registryError, and an unreadable shadwire.json becomes configError — always with exit code 0. Every field is listed under CLI. Without the CLI You can copy the files by hand from the published registry or from llms-full.txt, but shadwire.json then goes stale — and it is what makes diff, update and remove work. Prefer the CLI. Previous Introduction Next shadwire.json

title: shadwire.json
text: Docs Get started shadwire.json shadwire.json The manifest the CLI writes at your app's root. It is what lets diff, update and remove know what exists. shadwire init writes this file once. After that, every add, update and remove updates the installed section. Commit the file alongside your code. ExpandCopy{ "$schema": "https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/schema.json", "registry": "https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r", "tailwind": { "css": "app/assets/tailwind/application.css" }, "aliases": { "components": "app/components", "ui": "app/components/ui", "helpers": "app/helpers",{ "$schema": "https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/schema.json", "registry": "https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r", "tailwind": { "css": "app/assets/tailwind/application.css" }, "aliases": { "components": "app/components", "ui": "app/components/ui", "helpers": "app/helpers", "controllers": "app/javascript/controllers", "vendorCss": "vendor/shadwire" }, "installed": { "button": { "version": "0.2.0", "files": [ "app/components/ui/button_component.rb", "app/helpers/ui/button_helper.rb" ] } } } Fields Field What it is registry The base URL the CLI installs from. Persisted from init --registry. Accepts https:// and file://. tailwind.css The application's Tailwind entrypoint — the file that receives shadwire.css's @import. aliases Where each kind of file goes. Change these if your app does not follow the standard Rails tree. installed A per-component inventory: the registry version and the files it owns. It is the basis of diff, update and remove. Aliases Every registry file declares a kind (component, helper, Stimulus controller, CSS), and the matching alias decides its target directory. Alias Default Receives components app/components The shared UiComponent superclass. ui app/components/ui The component classes and their templates. helpers app/helpers The Ui::*Helper modules holding the ui_* wrappers. controllers app/javascript/controllers The Stimulus controllers of the interactive components. vendorCss vendor/shadwire shadwire.css, which carries the tokens. An app with a structure of its own, such as an engine, only has to point the aliases at the right directories before the first add: ExpandCopy{ "aliases": { "components": "app/components", "ui": "app/components/ui", "helpers": "app/helpers", "controllers": "app/javascript/controllers", "vendorCss": "app/assets/stylesheets/shadwire" },{ "aliases": { "components": "app/components", "ui": "app/components/ui", "helpers": "app/helpers", "controllers": "app/javascript/controllers", "vendorCss": "app/assets/stylesheets/shadwire" }, "tailwind": { "css": "app/assets/stylesheets/application.tailwind.css" } } Changing an alias after installing moves nothing The paths recorded in installed[].files keep pointing at wherever the files were written. If you need to change an alias with components already installed, remove them, adjust the alias, and install them again. The Tailwind @import init inserts the import into the file tailwind.css points at, and that import is what pulls the tokens into the build: Copy@import "tailwindcss"; @import "../../../vendor/shadwire/shadwire.css"; bin/shadwire status --json reports tailwind.importPresent. If it comes back false, the import is gone and the components will render with no colour. How the registry is resolved For any command, the base URL is resolved in this order: the --registry flag, if passed; the registry field of the app's shadwire.json; the built-in default, https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r. Copybin/shadwire add button --registry file://$PWD/build/r shadwire init --registry https://ui.example.com/r Passing --registry to init persists the choice to the file; on every other command it applies to that run alone. The format is documented under Registry. Previous Installation Next Theming

title: Theming
text: Docs Get started Theming Theming Every colour comes from a token. Retheming means editing two lists of CSS variables; no component has to change. Where the tokens live In vendor/shadwire/shadwire.css, installed by shadwire init and imported from the application's Tailwind entrypoint. bin/shadwire status --json reports the real path under tailwind.css. The file has three layers: ExpandCopy@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); /* dark mode por classe */ @theme inline { /* maps tokens to utilities */ --color-background: var(--background); --color-primary: var(--primary); /* ... */ }@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); /* dark mode por classe */ @theme inline { /* maps tokens to utilities */ --color-background: var(--background); --color-primary: var(--primary); /* ... */ } :root { --background: oklch(1 0 0); } /* valores do tema claro */ .dark { --background: oklch(0.145 0 0); } /* valores do tema escuro */ @theme inline is what turns --primary into the bg-primary and text-primary utilities. The colours are OKLCH. Edit :root and .dark, never @theme inline The @theme inline block is plumbing: it maps a variable to a utility. The theme itself lives in the :root (light) and .dark blocks. The tokens Every surface has a matching -foreground. Always use them as a pair: bg-muted text-muted-foreground, never bg-muted with the default text colour. Token Controls Used by background / foreground Application background and default text Page shell, sections, default text card / card-foreground Raised surfaces Card, dashboard and settings panels popover / popover-foreground Floating surfaces Popover, DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, overlays primary / primary-foreground High-emphasis actions, brand Default Button, selected states, badges secondary / secondary-foreground Lower-emphasis filled actions Secondary buttons and badges muted / muted-foreground Subtle surfaces, secondary content Descriptions, placeholders, empty states, supporting text accent / accent-foreground Hover, focus and active surfaces Ghost buttons, menu highlight, hovered rows destructive / destructive-foreground Destructive actions, errors Destructive buttons, invalid states border Borders and separators Cards, menus, tables, dividers input Form control borders Input, Textarea, Select, outline controls ring Focus rings Buttons, inputs, checkboxes, menus chart-1 … chart-5 Chart palette Charts and chart-driven blocks sidebar / sidebar-foreground Sidebar surface and text The Sidebar container sidebar-primary / -foreground High-emphasis actions in the sidebar Active items, icon tiles, CTAs sidebar-accent / -foreground Hover and selection in the sidebar Menu hover, open items sidebar-border Sidebar borders Sidebar headers, groups and dividers sidebar-ring Sidebar focus rings Focused controls in the sidebar radius Base corner radius Cards, inputs, buttons, popovers Changing the brand colour Set --primary and --primary-foreground in both blocks. Every component that uses bg-primary follows. ExpandCopy:root { --primary: oklch(0.55 0.22 264); --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0); } .dark { --primary: oklch(0.7 0.19 264); --primary-foreground: oklch(0.15 0 0);:root { --primary: oklch(0.55 0.22 264); --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0); } .dark { --primary: oklch(0.7 0.19 264); --primary-foreground: oklch(0.15 0 0); } Pick the foreground by its contrast against that surface, and check it in both modes. Adding a token Declare the variable in both blocks and map it in @theme inline so Tailwind generates the utilities: ExpandCopy@theme inline { --color-success: var(--success); --color-success-foreground: var(--success-foreground); } :root { --success: oklch(0.72 0.19 145); --success-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);@theme inline { --color-success: var(--success); --color-success-foreground: var(--success-foreground); } :root { --success: oklch(0.72 0.19 145); --success-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0); } .dark { --success: oklch(0.65 0.17 145); --success-foreground: oklch(0.15 0 0); } From then on bg-success and text-success-foreground behave like any other token. Corner radius --radius feeds the derived radius-sm / radius-md / radius-lg scale, so changing it reshapes cards, inputs, buttons and popovers at once. Copy:root { --radius: 0.75rem; } Adding a variant Variants are frozen Ruby hashes inside the component's class. Since the file is yours, adding one is adding a key: Copy# app/components/ui/button_component.rb VARIANTS = { default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground shadow-xs hover:bg-primary/90", success: "bg-success text-success-foreground shadow-xs hover:bg-success/90", # ... }.freeze Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :success) { "Publicar" } %> That is a local edit: bin/shadwire diff will report the file as modified, and bin/shadwire update would overwrite it. Keeping your edits bin/shadwire diff <name>: see what you changed. bin/shadwire update <name> without --yes: it asks about each modified file and shows the diff. Reapply your edits on top. Copybin/shadwire diff button # see what you changed bin/shadwire update button # without --yes: asks per file and shows the diff Prefer adding (a new variant key, a new token) over rewriting existing classes. Additive changes survive updates with far less conflict. Previous shadwire.json Next Dark mode

title: Dark mode
text: Docs Get started Dark mode Dark mode One class on <html> decides the whole theme. No component has to know about it. shadwire.css declares the dark variant anchored to a class: Copy@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); The dark variant fires when an ancestor carries the .dark class, so switching themes is toggling that class on <html>. Because every component uses tokens, and every token already has a value in both blocks, dark mode costs no component code at all. The toggle A five-line Stimulus controller. It is what switches the theme on this site: ExpandCopy// app/javascript/controllers/theme_controller.js import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus" export default class extends Controller { toggle() { const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark") localStorage.setItem("theme", isDark ? "dark" : "light") }// app/javascript/controllers/theme_controller.js import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus" export default class extends Controller { toggle() { const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark") localStorage.setItem("theme", isDark ? "dark" : "light") } } And the button, with the two icons swapping through the variant itself: Copy<%= ui_button(size: :icon, variant: :ghost, data: { controller: "theme", action: "theme#toggle" }, aria: { label: "Alternar tema" }) do %> <%= ui_icon("moon", class: "dark:hidden") %> <%= ui_icon("sun", class: "hidden dark:block") %> <% end %> dark:hidden and hidden dark:block decide which element shows, not what colour it is. That is the legitimate use of the dark: prefix. Avoiding the flash If the class is only applied once the application's JavaScript has loaded, anyone who chose the dark theme gets a white flash on every navigation. The fix is an inline script in <head>, ahead of any stylesheet, so it runs before the first paint: ExpandCopy<script> (() => { const stored = localStorage.getItem("theme") const dark = stored ? stored === "dark" : window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", dark) })()<script> (() => { const stored = localStorage.getItem("theme") const dark = stored ? stored === "dark" : window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", dark) })() </script> The order matters: the saved preference first, the system preference as the fallback. That way someone can choose light on a dark system and have the choice stick. Content Security Policy An app with a strict CSP has to allow this script, either through Rails' nonce (nonce: true on javascript_tag) or by moving it into a file loaded in <head> ahead of the stylesheets. Never write dark: for colour A hand-written override duplicates the colour decision and falls out of step with the theme the first time anyone touches the tokens: Copy<%# Wrong: light and dark colours written by hand %> <%= ui_card(class: "bg-white text-gray-900 dark:bg-gray-900 dark:text-white") do %> Copy<%# Right: the tokens already handle both modes %> <%= ui_card do %> If you need a colour the tokens do not cover, add a token. It gets a light and a dark value, and it keeps working through any future retheming. Testing both modes Theme bugs are almost never a literally wrong colour. They are usually a specificity collision between utilities of equal weight, or a missing companion utility: the class string looks right and the compiled CSS is not. When something looks off in the dark, read the generated CSS. Previous Theming Next CLI

title: CLI
text: Docs Tools CLI CLI The development-time tool that installs component source into your app and keeps it in step with the registry. After init, every command goes through bin/shadwire. The binstub resolves through the app's bundle, so everyone runs the same version of the CLI. Each command carries its own help under bin/shadwire help COMMAND. ExpandCopybin/shadwire status --json # the project's context bin/shadwire search <term> # find a component bin/shadwire info <name> --json # its full API bin/shadwire add <name> --yes # install it, dependencies included bin/shadwire list # the whole catalog bin/shadwire diff [name] # local drift bin/shadwire diff --exit-code # non-zero if there is drift (CI) bin/shadwire update [name] --yes # reapply the registry (overwrites!)bin/shadwire status --json # the project's context bin/shadwire search <term> # find a component bin/shadwire info <name> --json # its full API bin/shadwire add <name> --yes # install it, dependencies included bin/shadwire list # the whole catalog bin/shadwire diff [name] # local drift bin/shadwire diff --exit-code # non-zero if there is drift (CI) bin/shadwire update [name] --yes # reapply the registry (overwrites!) bin/shadwire remove <name> --yes # uninstall Commands Command What it does shadwire init Prepares the app: writes shadwire.json, installs the shared base files (ui_component.rb, shadwire.css) and the base gems, adds shadwire to the development group, creates the bin/shadwire binstub, and inserts the Tailwind @import. bin/shadwire add NAME... Installs one or more components along with their registry dependencies, applies gems and importmap pins, and records all of it in shadwire.json. bin/shadwire list Lists every component in the registry's catalog. bin/shadwire search QUERY Searches the catalog by name, title, description and when-to-use text, so conceptual terms like form, modal or loading work. bin/shadwire info NAME Shows the component's full API: helpers, variants, sizes, props, files, gems, pins and registry dependencies. bin/shadwire diff [NAME...] Compares the installed files against the registry and reports unchanged, modified or missing, with a unified diff for the modified ones. Read-only. bin/shadwire update [NAME...] Reapplies the registry's version of the installed components. Overwrites local edits, so run diff first. bin/shadwire remove NAME... Uninstalls components, deleting only the files exclusive to them — never the shared base, and never a file another installed component still uses. bin/shadwire status Describes the whole app in one call: detected stack, installed components with the helpers they define, and drift. bin/shadwire version Prints the installed version of the CLI. Reference status The project's context in a single call. It is the command to run first, and the only one an agent needs to inject. Copybin/shadwire status --json ExpandCopy{ "rails": true, "configPresent": true, "registryVersion": "0.2.0", "stack": { "importmap": true, "stimulus": true, "tailwindcssRails": true }, "gems": { "view_component": true, "lucide-rails": true }, "cli": { "gem": true, "binstub": true }, "tailwind": { "css": "app/assets/tailwind/application.css", "importPresent": true },{ "rails": true, "configPresent": true, "registryVersion": "0.2.0", "stack": { "importmap": true, "stimulus": true, "tailwindcssRails": true }, "gems": { "view_component": true, "lucide-rails": true }, "cli": { "gem": true, "binstub": true }, "tailwind": { "css": "app/assets/tailwind/application.css", "importPresent": true }, "helpers": { "includeAllHelpers": true, "legacyHelperPresent": false }, "installed": [ { "name": "card", "version": "0.2.0", "drift": "unchanged", "helpers": ["ui_card", "ui_card_header", "ui_card_title"], "classes": ["Ui::CardComponent", "Ui::Card::HeaderComponent"] } ], "availableCount": 58 } Field How to read it installed[].helpers The ui_* methods that actually exist in this app. Calling a helper for a component that is not installed raises NoMethodError. installed[].drift unchanged, modified, missing or unknown. stack.importmap Whether importmap and Stimulus are present. The interactive components need both. cli.binstub Whether bin/shadwire exists yet. False means running init once. helpers.includeAllHelpers False means the app turned off Rails' automatic helper inclusion: the Ui::*Helper modules then need a helper call per controller. helpers.legacyHelperPresent An app/helpers/ui_helper.rb left over from before the split by component. It defines helpers for components you do not have installed; it is safe to delete. search The search matches name, title, description and the when-to-use text, so conceptual terms work: form, modal, overlay, loading, right-click. Copybin/shadwire search form bin/shadwire search modal --json info The component's full API. Read it before writing ERB instead of guessing at a prop. It returns whenToUse, usage snippets, requiresStimulus, registryDependencies, the install files, and api.components[] with each class's helper, variants, sizes, props and attributes. Copybin/shadwire info dialog --json helper comes back null for anything without a ui_* wrapper: the base superclass, the internal parts a parent renders on its own, and the blocks. File bodies are omitted. add Copybin/shadwire add button dialog --yes Without --yes, files identical to the registry are skipped silently and only the locally modified ones prompt. In a non-interactive shell without --yes, everything is skipped and nothing gets installed. diff Read-only. Reports unchanged / modified / missing per file, with a unified diff for the modified ones. Copybin/shadwire diff bin/shadwire diff --json bin/shadwire diff --exit-code # non-zero when there is drift (fails CI) update Copybin/shadwire diff button # look first bin/shadwire update button --yes # then overwrite update overwrites local edits Run diff first. update does report what it replaced (overwritten and diffs in the JSON payload), but that is after the fact. See how to keep your edits. remove Copybin/shadwire remove chart --yes It deletes only the files exclusive to the components being removed. The shared base, and any file another installed component still uses, stays where it is. Importmap pins nobody uses any more are reported, not removed. Flags Flag Commands Effect --cwd DIR all Runs against another application directory instead of the current one. --registry URL all Reads from another registry. Accepts https:// and file://, which is how you test a locally built registry. --json all but version Emits machine-readable JSON instead of human output. This is what agents and CI use. --yes, -y init, add, update, remove Applies file and dependency changes without asking. --overwrite add, update Overwrites locally modified files without asking. --no-deps add, update Skips transitive registry dependencies (on by default). --force init Rewrites an existing shadwire.json and recreates the binstub. --exit-code diff Exits non-zero when there is drift, so CI can fail on it. Errors and exit codes Exit code 0 means it worked. A command that could not install a dependency says so and exits non-zero, so you can trust the exit code instead of re-reading the Gemfile. Copy$ shadwire init --yes Initialized shadwire (2 base files). create app/components/ui_component.rb FAILED view_component (bundle add failed) Failed to install: view_component. Run `bundle add view_component` in the app and re-run this command. $ echo $? 1 Each error comes out as one actionable line on stderr. A malformed shadwire.json, an unreachable registry, a registry serving HTML and a missing argument each produce their own: Copyshadwire.json is not valid JSON: expected object key, got 'not' at line 1 column 3 Could not reach the registry at https://…/index.json: getaddrinfo(3): Name or service not known add requires at least one component name The exception is status, which never fails: it reports "rails": false, registryError or configError as fields and exits 0. That is what makes it safe to inject anywhere. In CI Every command runs non-interactively with --yes, emits JSON with --json, and points at another directory with --cwd. This recipe fails the build when an installed component has diverged from the registry: Copy- name: Install dependencies (with the development group) run: bundle install # Fails when an installed file has diverged from the registry. - name: Checar drift do Shadwire run: bin/shadwire diff --exit-code The job needs the development group installed; without it, bin/shadwire does not exist. title: Agent skill
headings: The skill does not list components
text: Docs Tools Agent skill Agent skill An installable skill that teaches coding agents to use Shadwire: the workflow, the rules, and your app's API, read at the moment it is needed. An agent writing ERB with no context invents props: it guesses icon: on a button, calls ui_carousel in an app where the carousel is not installed, writes bg-blue-500 where a token exists. The skill carries the workflow and the conventions, and pulls the data — component names, variants, props, helpers — from the CLI itself, at the point of use. Copynpx skills add edumoraes/shadwire The skills installer covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and around twenty other agents. The skill lives at skills/shadwire/ in the repository. The skill does not list components A skill that listed the components and their variants would go stale on the first add, with nothing to announce it. Instead it injects the output of bin/shadwire status --json as project context and tells the agent to read that before anything else. Copy## Current Project Context ```! bin/shadwire status --json 2>/dev/null || bundle exec shadwire status --json 2>/dev/null || … ``` The block always returns parseable JSON. Three fields decide what the agent may write: Field Why it decides installed[].helpers The ui_* methods that exist in this app. Calling the helper of a component that is not installed raises NoMethodError. stack.importmap Whether the interactive components will work at all. 29 of the 57 components ship a Stimulus controller. cli.binstub Whether bin/shadwire exists yet. False means running init once before anything else. The repository's CI checks that everything the skill names still exists in the registry and in the CLI, and runs the workflow it teaches end to end — so a stale skill breaks the build. What it carries File Contents SKILL.md Principles, critical rules, the component selection table and the workflow. Injects bin/shadwire status --json as project context. cli.md A reference for every command and flag, the shape of the JSON payload, and how to read errors and exit codes. theming.md Where the tokens live, class-based dark mode, how to retheme, how to add a token, and how to keep edits across updates. rules/composition.md Subcomponents as nested helpers, items inside their group, mandatory titles on overlays, Stimulus. rules/styling.md Semantic tokens, class precedence, free-form HTML attributes, Tailwind utility conventions. rules/forms.md The field family, validation state, wiring into form_with, and choosing the control. rules/icons.md lucide-rails, kebab-case names, sizes, and when an icon needs an accessible label. SKILL.md is the front door; the rest are references it links to. The same rules are documented here under Composition, Styling, Forms and Icons. The workflow it teaches Copybin/shadwire status --json # 1. what already exists in this app bin/shadwire search modal # 2. find the component bin/shadwire info dialog --json # 3. read the API before writing ERB bin/shadwire add dialog --yes # 4. instalar bin/shadwire status --json # 5. confirm the new helpers info --json returns the helper names, the variants and the sizes. It is the step most often skipped, and without it the agent reinvents the component out of divs and utilities. Trust the exit code A non-zero exit means something was not applied (almost always a bundle add), and the message says how to recover. The skill instructs the agent to stop there rather than carry on as if it had worked. Permissions The skill's frontmatter declares the tools it needs: Copy--- name: shadwire description: Manages shadcn/ui components in Ruby on Rails apps via the shadwire CLI… user-invocable: false allowed-tools: Bash(bin/shadwire *), Bash(./bin/shadwire *), Bash(bundle exec shadwire *), Bash(shadwire *) --- That allowed-tools applies only to the turn that invokes the skill. To silence the permission prompts, add a rule to the application's .claude/settings.json: Copy{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(bin/shadwire *)"] } } user-invocable: false is deliberate: nobody types this skill. It is the context the agent loads when the subject is UI in a Rails app that has a shadwire.json. Agents without the skill Not every agent installs skills. The same catalog is published in plain text, in the llms.txt format: an index saying when to use each component, and a file carrying the whole API. Either one can be pasted straight into a model's context. Previous CLI Next Registry

title: Registry
text:
Docs Tools Registry Registry Static JSON files served over HTTP, with no application server and no authentication. It is what the CLI reads. Shadwire's published registry lives at shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r. There are two kinds of document: an index carrying the catalog, and one file per item with the contents of each of its files inlined. URL Contents /r/index.json The catalog (name, title, description, when to use) and `base`: the shared files and gems that init installs. /r/{name}.json One component: metadata, resolved registry dependencies, the extracted API, and the files with their contents inlined. /r/llms.txt The same catalog in plain text, for agents. /r/llms-full.txt Every component's full API in plain text. Copycurl -s https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r/index.json | jq '.items | length' curl -s https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r/button.json | jq '.api.components[0].variants' index.json What list and search read, and where init gets the base installation from. ExpandCopy{ "name": "shadwire", "version": "0.2.0", "items": [ { "name": "button", "type": "component", "title": "Button",{ "name": "shadwire", "version": "0.2.0", "items": [ { "name": "button", "type": "component", "title": "Button", "description": "Displays a button or a link styled as a button.", "whenToUse": "Any clickable action. Use tag: :a for a link that looks like a button…" } ], "base": { "files": [{ "target": "app/components/ui_component.rb", "type": "component", "content": "…" }], "gems": ["view_component", "lucide-rails"], "tailwind": { "version": "4", "css": "shadwire.css" } } } One item Each item carries enough to install without a second request, file contents included. registryDependencies arrives with its transitive closure already resolved, so the CLI never has to walk the graph. ExpandCopy{ "name": "button", "type": "component", "title": "Button", "description": "Displays a button or a link styled as a button.", "whenToUse": "Any clickable action…", "usage": ["<%= ui_button(variant: :outline, size: :sm) { "Save" } %>"], "gems": [],{ "name": "button", "type": "component", "title": "Button", "description": "Displays a button or a link styled as a button.", "whenToUse": "Any clickable action…", "usage": ["<%= ui_button(variant: :outline, size: :sm) { "Save" } %>"], "gems": [], "importmap": [], "registryDependencies": ["icon"], "requiresStimulus": false, "api": { "components": [ { "class": "Ui::ButtonComponent", "helper": "ui_button", "root": true, "variants": ["default", "destructive", "outline", "secondary", "ghost", "link"], "sizes": ["default", "sm", "lg", "icon"], "props": [{ "name": "tag", "default": ":button" }] } ] }, "files": [ { "target": "app/components/ui/button_component.rb", "type": "component", "content": "# frozen_string_literal: true

module Ui
 class ButtonComponent…" } ] } Field What it is whenToUse One sentence on when to reach for this component and what its neighbours are. It is the text search matches against. usage Ready-made ERB snippets for the most common case. registryDependencies Other items that have to come along, transitive closure included. requiresStimulus True when the item installs a controller under app/javascript/. api.components[] Extracted from the source: class, helper, variants, sizes, props and attributes. files[] Each file as { target, type, content }, with no source paths. How it is built The source of truth is registry/registry.json in the monorepo, which lists each item's files as source → target pairs. bin/build_registry turns that into the published registry, inlining the contents and extracting the API from the source: Copybin/build_registry # registry/registry.json → build/r/{name}.json + index.json ls build/r | head The output goes to build/, which is generated and never hand-edited. CI rebuilds it on every push to main, alongside this site's deploy. Serving your own Because these are static files, any host will do: a bucket, a Pages site, a directory behind a proxy. Point the CLI at it with --registry, or persist the choice into shadwire.json by passing the flag to init. file:// bases work too, which is how you test a registry built locally: Copybin/build_registry bin/shadwire add button --registry "file://$PWD/build/r" The registry URL is written into the user's app shadwire.json keeps the URL used at init time. Existing installs go on pointing at the old address, so moving a published registry means keeping a redirect in place. Previous Agent skill Next llms.txt

title: llms.txt
text: Docs Tools llms.txt llms.txt The same catalog in plain text, for when the agent has neither the skill nor a way to run the CLI. The agent skill is the preferred route: it reads the app and knows what is installed. But not every agent installs skills, and not every context has a shell. For those, the registry build publishes two plain-text variants, generated from the same data. File Contents When to use it /r/llms.txt Every component with its title, description and when-to-use text. Choosing the right component. Fits comfortably in any context window. /r/llms-full.txt The above plus the full API: helpers, variants, sizes, props and usage snippets. Writing ERB with no way to consult the CLI. Copycurl -s https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r/llms.txt curl -s https://shadwire.edumoraes.dev.br/r/llms-full.txt Format Plain Markdown, following the llms.txt convention: a title, a short summary, and sections by area — how to install, the licence the source arrives under, and the catalog itself. ExpandCopy# shadwire 0.2.0 shadcn/ui components for Ruby on Rails, delivered as source your app owns. Components are copied into the app by the CLI; there is no runtime dependency on Shadwire. ## Install# shadwire 0.2.0 shadcn/ui components for Ruby on Rails, delivered as source your app owns. Components are copied into the app by the CLI; there is no runtime dependency on Shadwire. ## Install gem install shadwire # or: bundle add shadwire --group development shadwire init # writes shadwire.json and the shared base files shadwire add <name> # installs a component and its dependencies ## Licence MIT — https://github.com/edumoraes/shadwire/blob/main/LICENSE Ported from shadcn/ui (https://ui.shadcn.com), MIT. ## Components - button — Any clickable action. Use tag: :a for a link that looks like a button, size: :icon for icon-only… The limitation These files describe the registry, not your app. They list all 57 components, including the ones you never installed — and the helper of a component you did not install does not exist. Installing by hand leaves shadwire.json inaccurate You can copy the code out of llms-full.txt, but the inventory in shadwire.json is not updated — and that inventory is what makes diff, update and remove work. If the CLI is available, use the CLI. Previous Registry Next Composition

title: Composition
headings: Helpers exist only for what is installed
text:
Docs Guides Composition Composition Subcomponents are nested helpers, not props. The view's structure mirrors the HTML's, exactly as in shadcn/ui. Helpers exist only for what is installed Each component installs its own helper module: button writes app/helpers/ui/button_helper.rb, which defines Ui::ButtonHelper#ui_button. Rails automatically includes everything under app/helpers/, so an installed helper is available in every view with no include. The helper of a component that is not installed does not exist, and calling it raises NoMethodError at request time. Check installed[].helpers before you write. Copybin/shadwire status --json bin/shadwire add carousel --yes A leftover ui_helper.rb at the root? Older installs had a single app/helpers/ui_helper.rb. It defines helpers for components that may not be installed. status --json reports it under helpers.legacyHelperPresent; the file is safe to delete. Subcomponents are nested helpers There are no ViewComponent slots and no content props in this code. Composition happens through nested calls. Copy<%# Wrong: these props do not exist %> <%= ui_card(header: "Time", footer: "Save") %> ExpandCopy<%# Right %> <%= ui_card do %> <%= ui_card_header do %> <%= ui_card_title { "Time" } %> <%= ui_card_description { "Gerencie quem tem acesso." } %> <% end %> <%= ui_card_content { "Corpo" } %> <%= ui_card_footer { ui_button { "Save" } } %><%# Right %> <%= ui_card do %> <%= ui_card_header do %> <%= ui_card_title { "Time" } %> <%= ui_card_description { "Gerencie quem tem acesso." } %> <% end %> <%= ui_card_content { "Corpo" } %> <%= ui_card_footer { ui_button { "Save" } } %> <% end %> bin/shadwire info lists each item's subcomponent helpers. Do not invent names: the helper is ui_card_content, not ui_card_body. Use the whole composition Do not collapse a component into a single part. Header, title and description carry semantics; dumping everything into the content throws that away. Copy<%# Wrong: everything dumped into the content %> <%= ui_card do %> <%= ui_card_content do %>

Time

Gerencie quem tem acesso.

<% end %> <% end %> Items go inside their group Copy<%# Wrong: item rendered straight at the root %> <%= ui_select do %> <%= ui_select_item(value: "a") { "A" } %> <% end %> Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_select(name: "role", placeholder: "Escolha um papel") do %> <%= ui_select_trigger { ui_select_value } %> <%= ui_select_content do %> <%= ui_select_item(value: "admin") { "Admin" } %> <% end %> <% end %> The same holds for ui_tabs_trigger inside ui_tabs_list, ui_breadcrumb_item inside ui_breadcrumb_list, and ui_pagination_item inside ui_pagination_content. Overlays always need a title dialog, alert-dialog, sheet and drawer need their title component for screen readers, even when the design shows none. Copy<%# Wrong: the dialog has no accessible name %> <%= ui_dialog_content do %>

Tem certeza?

<% end %> Copy<%# Right: visually hidden, but announced %> <%= ui_dialog_content do %> <%= ui_dialog_header do %> <%= ui_dialog_title(class: "sr-only") { "Confirm deletion" } %> <% end %>

Tem certeza?

<% end %> Interactive components need Stimulus 29 of the 57 components ship a controller. bin/shadwire info reports requiresStimulus, and status.stack says whether the app has importmap and stimulus-rails. The controllers install into app/javascript/controllers/ and register themselves through controllers/index.js's eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", application). If your app registers controllers explicitly, register the new ones there too. Rendering the class directly The helper is a thin wrapper. The two forms are equivalent: Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :outline) { "Save" } %> <%= render Ui::ButtonComponent.new(variant: :outline) do %>Save<% end %> Prefer the helper in views. Reach for the class when you need the component object itself, or when you are inside another ViewComponent. Components do not get helpers automatically, so include the module to call ui_button from a template: Copyclass DashboardCardComponent < ViewComponent::Base # Components do not get helpers automatically. include Ui::ButtonHelper end Previous llms.txt Next Styling

title: Styling
headings: class: and class_name: are the same thing
Prefer variants and sizes over utilities
text: Docs Guides Styling Styling Variants for appearance, class: for layout. Every colour comes from a token, and your class always wins. Semantic tokens only Every colour comes from a shadcn token, so light mode, dark mode and any retheming work without touching component code. Copy<%# Wrong: hardcoded colours and a hand-written dark override %> <%= ui_card(class: "bg-white text-gray-900 dark:bg-gray-900 dark:text-white") do %> Copy<%# Right: the tokens already cover both modes %> <%= ui_card do %> The pairs are <surface> / <surface>-foreground: bg-primary text-primary-foreground, bg-muted text-muted-foreground, bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground. The full table is under Theming. Never write dark: variants for colour. Use the prefix only for mode-specific choices that are not colour, such as a different image. class: and class_name: are the same thing Both normalise to the same value. Use whichever reads better; class: is the more idiomatic Rails. Copy<%= ui_button(class: "w-full") { "Save" } %> <%= ui_button(class_name: "w-full") { "Save" } %> Your class always wins Classes compose in this order, with yours last: Copybase_classes → variant_classes → size_classes → a sua class That is why class: overrides the component's utilities. Even so, do not use it to restyle: Copy<%# Wrong: fighting the design system %> <%= ui_button(class: "bg-red-600 hover:bg-red-700") { "Delete" } %> Copy<%# Right: the variant already exists %> <%= ui_button(variant: :destructive) { "Delete" } %> Use class: for layout: width, margin, position in a grid. Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :outline, class: "w-full sm:w-auto") { "Save" } %> HTML attributes pass straight through Anything that is not a known prop is forwarded to the rendered element, Rails' nested hashes included. Copy<%= ui_button(id: "save", data: { turbo: false, controller: "form" }, "aria-describedby": "hint") { "Save" } %> <%= ui_button(tag: :a, href: post_path(post), data: { turbo_method: :delete }) { "Delete" } %> Use tag: to swap the element where the component supports it. button renders a <button> by default and an <a> with tag: :a. Prefer variants and sizes over utilities Look at what already exists before writing classes: Copy$ bin/shadwire info button variants: default | destructive | outline | secondary | ghost | link sizes: default | sm | lg | icon Copy<%# Wrong %> <%= ui_button(class: "h-8 px-3 text-xs border") { "Pequeno" } %> Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_button(variant: :outline, size: :sm) { "Pequeno" } %> Utility conventions Follow what the components themselves do, so your code does not read differently from what the CLI installed: size-9 rather than h-9 w-9, when width and height match. gap-* with flex or grid, rather than space-x-* / space-y-*. truncate rather than overflow-hidden text-ellipsis whitespace-nowrap. no manual z-index on overlays: dialog, sheet, popover and dropdown-menu already manage their own stacking. Previous Composition Next Forms

title: Forms
headings: There is no form builder integration
The date picker is a recipe
Input group brings its own input
text:
Docs Guides Forms Forms field is the layout primitive for a form row. There is no form builder integration. Wrap every control in ui_field Never build a form row out of divs and spacing utilities. field already handles the label, the description, the error and the space between them. Copy<%# Wrong %>
<%= ui_label(for: "email") { "Email" } %> <%= ui_input(type: :email, id: "email", name: "email") %>

Nunca compartilhamos.

Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_field do %> <%= ui_field_label(for: "email") { "Email" } %> <%= ui_input(type: :email, id: "email", name: "email") %> <%= ui_field_description { "Nunca compartilhamos." } %> <% end %> The whole family: Helper Role ui_field The row. Takes orientation: :vertical (default), :horizontal or :responsive. ui_field_group Stacks several fields with consistent spacing. ui_field_set + ui_field_legend Groups related checkboxes or radios, in place of a div with a heading. ui_field_label The field's label. ui_field_title / ui_field_description Supporting text above and below the control. ui_field_error The error message, with role="alert". ui_field_content Wraps the control when it needs a container of its own. ui_field_separator Divides sections inside a group. Validation state Pass invalid: true to ui_field. It sets data-invalid and turns the row's text destructive; the message goes in ui_field_error. Copy<%= ui_field(invalid: user.errors[:email].any?) do %> <%= ui_field_label(for: "email") { "Email" } %> <%= ui_input(type: :email, id: "email", name: "email", "aria-invalid": user.errors[:email].any?) %> <%= ui_field_error(errors: user.errors[:email]) %> <% end %> ui_field_error takes either block content or an array in errors:, and renders nothing when both are empty — so you can leave it permanently in place, with no conditional. There is no form builder integration There is no f.ui_input. The controls accept free-form HTML attributes and forward them to the element, so you wire them to form_with by hand: ExpandCopy<%= form_with(model: @user) do |form| %> <%= ui_field(invalid: @user.errors[:email].any?) do %> <%= ui_field_label(for: form.field_id(:email)) { "Email" } %> <%= ui_input(type: :email, id: form.field_id(:email), name: form.field_name(:email), value: @user.email) %> <%= ui_field_error(errors: @user.errors[:email]) %><%= form_with(model: @user) do |form| %> <%= ui_field(invalid: @user.errors[:email].any?) do %> <%= ui_field_label(for: form.field_id(:email)) { "Email" } %> <%= ui_input(type: :email, id: form.field_id(:email), name: form.field_name(:email), value: @user.email) %> <%= ui_field_error(errors: @user.errors[:email]) %> <% end %> <%= ui_button(type: :submit) { "Save" } %> <% end %> form.field_name and form.field_id produce the user[email] / user_email pair Rails expects, so the params arrive as usual. The same holds for ui_checkbox, ui_switch, ui_textarea, ui_select, ui_radio_group and ui_slider. Checkbox does not emit Rails' hidden input Unlike form.check_box, there is no hidden field carrying the unchecked value. Treat a missing parameter as unchecked, or declare the hidden input yourself when the form has to submit a value either way: Copy<%= hidden_field_tag form.field_name(:admin), "0", id: nil %> <%= ui_checkbox(name: form.field_name(:admin), id: form.field_id(:admin), value: "1", checked: @user.admin?) %> Choosing the control Situation Control One line of text ui_input Several lines ui_textarea Text with a prefix, suffix or button ui_input_group One of a long list ui_select, or combobox when it needs searching One of a few visible options ui_radio_group The native mobile picker, no JS ui_native_select Several independent choices ui_checkbox Two to seven compact choices ui_toggle_group A setting applied immediately ui_switch An imprecise number ui_slider An exact number ui_input(type: :number) A date or a range date-picker, or ui_calendar inline A one-time code ui_input_otp The date picker is a recipe There is no Ui::DatePickerComponent. A date field is ui_popover + ui_calendar, with the ui-date-picker controller writing the chosen date into the trigger and closing the popover. The calendar owns the value: name: renders the hidden input, so it submits like any other field. ExpandCopy
<%= ui_popover do %> <%= ui_popover_trigger(variant: :outline, class: "w-[212px] justify-between font-normal") do %> Escolha uma data <%= ui_icon("chevron-down", class: "opacity-50") %> <% end %> <%= ui_popover_content(align: :start, class: "w-auto! p-0!") do %>
<%= ui_popover do %> <%= ui_popover_trigger(variant: :outline, class: "w-[212px] justify-between font-normal") do %> Escolha uma data <%= ui_icon("chevron-down", class: "opacity-50") %> <% end %> <%= ui_popover_content(align: :start, class: "w-auto! p-0!") do %> <%= ui_calendar(name: "due_on") %> <% end %> <% end %>
The popover needs w-auto! p-0!, because the default w-72 with padding is too narrow for the grid. The variations are calendar arguments: mode: :range, caption_layout: :dropdown, dir: :rtl. bin/shadwire info date-picker prints them all, and the Date Picker page shows each one live. Input group brings its own input Inside ui_input_group, use its own helpers, not a bare ui_input. Copy<%# Wrong %> <%= ui_input_group do %> <%= ui_input_group_addon { ui_icon("search") } %> <%= ui_input(name: "q") %> <% end %> Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_input_group do %> <%= ui_input_group_addon { ui_icon("search") } %> <%= ui_input_group_input(name: "q", placeholder: "Buscar") %> <% end %> Previous Styling Next Icons

title: Icons
text: Docs Guides Icons Icons Icons come from lucide-rails, the Rails port of Lucide (shadcn/ui's set). ui_icon wraps lucide_icon with shadcn's size variants. The application needs the lucide-rails gem. shadwire init adds it, and bin/shadwire status --json reports it under gems. Names are Lucide's kebab-case Copy<%# Wrong: React component names do not exist here %> <%= ui_icon("ChevronDown") %> <%= ui_icon(:chevron_down) %> Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_icon("chevron-down") %> The names are listed at lucide.dev/icons. Sizes Size Class Typical use :sm size-3 Inside badges, supporting text and breadcrumbs. :default size-4 Buttons, menu items, fields. :lg size-5 Headings, tiles, empty states. :xl size-6 Illustrations and feature callouts. Copy<%= ui_icon("check", size: :sm) %> Prefer these sizes over class: "w-3 h-3", so the icon follows any future adjustment to the scale. Icons are decorative by default ui_icon renders aria-hidden="true", which is right beside a text label, since the text is what names the control. Copy<%# Right: "Download" is already the label; the icon is decoration %> <%= ui_button { safe_join([ ui_icon("download"), " Baixar" ]) } %> When the icon is the only content, it has to carry the name. Pass label:, which sets role="img" and aria-label and cancels the aria-hidden: Copy<%# Wrong: icon-only button with no accessible name %> <%= ui_button(size: :icon) { ui_icon("trash-2") } %> Copy<%# Right: either of these works %> <%= ui_button(size: :icon) { ui_icon("trash-2", label: "Delete") } %> <%= ui_button(size: :icon, "aria-label": "Delete") { ui_icon("trash-2") } %> Labelling the button instead of the icon is equally valid; what is not allowed is neither. There is no icon: prop No component takes an icon as a prop. The icon goes in the content, shadcn-style. Copy<%# Wrong: no component has that prop %> <%= ui_button(icon: "plus") { "Adicionar" } %> Copy<%# Right %> <%= ui_button { safe_join([ ui_icon("plus"), " Adicionar" ]) } %> ButtonComponent carries [&_svg] utilities, so a nested icon comes out sized and spaced with no extra class. Use size: :icon for an icon-only button. Both parts have to be html_safe, so join them with safe_join rather than concatenating strings. ui_icon("save") + " Save" works too, since the icon is safe, but safe_join states the intent and handles interpolated content correctly. Previous Forms Next Accessibility

title: Accessibility
text:
Docs Guides Accessibility Accessibility The components follow the WAI-ARIA APG patterns and prefer the native element wherever one exists. What is left for you is short. What comes built in Area What the component already does Native element first Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet and Drawer use the native : focus trapping, Esc and focus restoration come from the browser. Checkbox, Radio Group and Switch are styled native inputs. Roles and states Tabs exposes tablist/tab/tabpanel; Select is an APG combobox with aria-activedescendant; Toggle uses aria-pressed; Progress exposes aria-valuenow. Keyboard Arrow keys navigate menus, tabs, select and toggle group; typeahead matches by prefix in menus and select; Esc closes overlays. Visible focus Every interactive control carries the focus ring from the ring token, including the :focus-visible state. Decoration is hidden Icons render aria-hidden="true" by default; decorative separators leave the accessibility tree. Every component has render tests in the repository, and an accessibility suite walks the site's pages checking structure, labelling and navigation. The system tests run in headless Chrome on every change. What stays yours Naming overlays gives you focus and keyboard handling, but it does not invent a name. Every dialog, sheet and drawer needs its title component; use class: "sr-only" when the design shows none. Copy<%= ui_dialog_content do %> <%= ui_dialog_header do %> <%= ui_dialog_title(class: "sr-only") { "Confirm deletion" } %> <% end %>

This action cannot be undone.

<% end %> Naming icons that carry meaning An icon beside text is decoration and should stay hidden. An icon on its own becomes the label, so pass label: or label the control that contains it. Details under Icons. Copy<%= ui_icon("bell", label: "Notifications") %> Tying label to control Since there is no form builder integration, the for: / id: pair is yours. ui_field lays the row out, but it does not guess the control's id. See Forms. Contrast after retheming The default values pass the contrast criteria; yours have to be checked. Always set the / -foreground pair together, and test in both modes. Heading hierarchy ui_card_title and ui_dialog_title are style, not level. If the page needs a heading structure, write the h1–h3 around them yourself. Testing in your app The installed components are your code, so they test like any ViewComponent. Pin the accessible name in a test — that is the part the library cannot guarantee on its own: Copytest "dialog renders a native with an accessible name" do render_inline(Ui::Dialog::ContentComponent.new) do render_inline(Ui::Dialog::TitleComponent.new) { "Edit profile" } end assert_selector "dialog[aria-labelledby]" assert_text "Edit profile" end Interactive components need a browser Focus, keyboard handling and behaviour only show up in a system test. A render test confirms the markup, not that Esc closes anything. Found a problem? Broken accessibility in a component is a registry bug, not a bug in your app: open an issue. In the meantime the file is yours, so fix it locally and run bin/shadwire diff before your next update. Previous Icons Next Localisation

title: Localisation
headings: Four of them are read by JavaScript
Month and day names come from Rails
text: Docs Guides Localisation Localisation Installed components read their user-facing strings from I18n with English defaults. An app that defines nothing gets English; an app that defines the key gets its own text. Every string a component renders on its own — a close button's label, a pagination arrow, an empty-table message — goes through I18n.t with the English text as the default: Copy# app/components/ui/dialog/content_component.rb, as installed I18n.t("ui.dialog.close", default: "Close") That default is what makes an install work with no setup: the component renders English in an app with no locale file for it at all. Nothing has to be configured before a component is usable, and nothing breaks in an app that never touches I18n. Overriding a string Define the key in your own locale file. There is no registration step and no component prop — the key is the API. ExpandCopy# config/locales/pt.yml pt: ui: dialog: close: Fechar sheet: close: Fechar pagination:# config/locales/pt.yml pt: ui: dialog: close: Fechar sheet: close: Fechar pagination: previous: Anterior next: Próxima Only the keys you define are overridden; the rest keep their English defaults, so you can translate a component at a time. The keys Every key a component reads, with the text it falls back to. Keys marked value are rendered into a data-*-value attribute and read by a Stimulus controller rather than printed by the server — see below. breadcrumb Key Default Kind ui.breadcrumb.more More server calendar Key Default Kind ui.calendar.month Month value ui.calendar.next_month Next month server ui.calendar.previous_month Previous month server ui.calendar.year Year value carousel Key Default Kind ui.carousel.next Next slide server ui.carousel.previous Previous slide server data_table Key Default Kind ui.data_table.columns Columns server ui.data_table.empty No results. server ui.data_table.filter_placeholder Filter… server ui.data_table.next Next server ui.data_table.previous Previous server ui.data_table.select_all Select all rows server ui.data_table.select_row Select row server ui.data_table.selection %{selected} of %{total} row(s) selected. value dialog Key Default Kind ui.dialog.close Close server pagination Key Default Kind ui.pagination.more More pages server ui.pagination.next Next server ui.pagination.next_label Go to the next page server ui.pagination.previous Previous server ui.pagination.previous_label Go to the previous page server sheet Key Default Kind ui.sheet.close Close server sonner Key Default Kind ui.sonner.close Close value ui.sonner.label Notifications server spinner Key Default Kind ui.spinner.label Loading server Four of them are read by JavaScript ui.data_table.selection, ui.calendar.month, ui.calendar.year and ui.sonner.close are not printed into the page. They are resolved once, when the component renders, and written into a data-*-value attribute the controller reads. Translating them works exactly the same way — they are still ordinary I18n keys. One of them carries a trap. The data table's selection count is interpolated by the controller, not by I18n, so both tokens have to survive the translation: Copypt: ui: data_table: # %{selected} and %{total} are substituted by the Stimulus # controller, not by I18n. Keep both tokens, in any order. selection: "%{selected} de %{total} linha(s) selecionada(s)." Translating or dropping %{selected} or %{total} leaves the caption with a literal token or no numbers at all, and nothing reports it — I18n never sees these placeholders. Month and day names come from Rails The calendar's caption and column headers are not in the ui. namespace. They are props, so they can come from Rails' own date translations — which your app already has if it loads a locale from rails-i18n: Copy<%= ui_calendar(month_names: I18n.t("date.month_names").compact, day_names: I18n.t("date.abbr_day_names")) %> .compact matters: Rails' date.month_names is 1-indexed and starts with a nil. A worked example This site is the example. Its Portuguese pages render the same components you install, with the whole ui. block defined once — which is why every string the components supply themselves on /pt (close buttons, pagination arrows, the empty-table message) reads in Portuguese. sandbox/config/locales/pt.yml carries every key on this page, and is a copy-paste starting point for a Portuguese app. Previous Accessibility Next Overview

text: Docs Components Overview Components ViewComponent ports of the shadcn/ui components. Open any page for live examples, usage code and the API reference. 57 components Install any of them with bin/shadwire add <name>. See Installation. Accordion → Vertically stacked sections that expand and collapse. Alert → A callout for important inline messages. Alert Dialog → A modal that interrupts the user to confirm a consequential action. Aspect Ratio → Constrains its content to a fixed width-to-height ratio. Avatar → A user or entity image with a text fallback. Badge → A small inline label for status, counts, or categories. Breadcrumb → A trail showing the current page's position in the hierarchy. Button → Displays a button or a link styled as a button. Button Group → Related buttons joined into a single control. Calendar → A month grid for selecting a date or a date range. Card → A container for grouping related content with header, body, and footer slots. Carousel → A horizontally or vertically swipeable set of slides. Chart → Chart.js charts using the Shadwire theme tokens. Checkbox → A binary control for opting in or selecting many items. Collapsible → A single region that expands and collapses. Combobox → A searchable single-select built from popover, command, and button. Command → A searchable, keyboard-driven list of commands. Context Menu → A menu opened by right-clicking a region. Data Table → A table with sorting, filtering, pagination, and row selection. Date Picker → A date field that opens a calendar in a popover. Dialog → A modal window overlaying the page. Drawer → A panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen. Dropdown Menu → A menu of actions or options triggered by a button. Empty → A placeholder for when there is nothing to show. Field → Form field layout with label, description, and error message. Hover Card → A rich preview card shown on hover. Icon → A Lucide icon with shadcn-style size variants. Input → A single-line text field. Input Group → An input with attached addons, text, or buttons. Input OTP → A segmented field for one-time passcodes. Item → A compact row with media, text, and trailing actions. Kbd → Displays a keyboard key or shortcut. Label → An accessible caption bound to a form control. Menubar → A horizontal application menu bar. Native Select → The browser's native select element, styled to match. Navigation Menu → Site navigation with optional rich dropdown panels. Pagination → Navigation controls for moving between pages of results. Popover → A floating panel anchored to a trigger. Progress → A bar showing completion toward a known total. Radio Group → A set of mutually exclusive options. Resizable → Panels the user can resize by dragging a handle. Scroll Area → A scrollable region with styled scrollbars. Select → A styled control for choosing one option from a list. Separator → A thin rule that visually divides content. Sheet → A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen. Sidebar → A composable, collapsible application sidebar. Skeleton → A placeholder block shown while content loads. Slider → Selects a numeric value from a range by dragging. Sonner → Transient toast notifications. Spinner → An indeterminate loading indicator. Switch → A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately. Table → A styled HTML table with header, body, and footer sections. Tabs → Switches between peer views in the same space. Textarea → A multi-line text field. Toggle → A two-state button that stays pressed. Toggle Group → A set of toggle buttons acting as one control. Tooltip → A short hint shown on hover or focus. Button Copy<%= ui_button { "Button" } %> Secondary A lower-emphasis alternative for secondary actions. Secondary Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :secondary) { "Secondary" } %> Destructive For destructive actions, such as deleting a record. Destructive Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :destructive) { "Destructive" } %> Outline Border only, no fill — good for neutral actions. Outline Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :outline) { "Outline" } %> Ghost No background and no border until hover. Ghost Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :ghost) { "Ghost" } %> Link Looks like a text link while keeping button semantics. Link Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :link) { "Link" } %> Icon A square icon-only button (size: :icon). Pass label: on the icon for screen readers. Copy<%= ui_button(size: :icon, variant: :secondary) do %> <%= ui_icon("chevron-right", label: "Next") %> <% end %> With icon Compose ui_icon inside the block; the button sizes the SVG for you. Baixar Copy<%= ui_button do %> <%= ui_icon("download") %> Baixar <% end %> Sizes The :sm, :default and :lg sizes side by side. Small Default Large Copy<%= ui_button(size: :sm) { "Small" } %> <%= ui_button(size: :default) { "Default" } %> <%= ui_button(size: :lg) { "Large" } %> Loading A loading state composed from a spinning icon and disabled. Carregando Copy<%= ui_button(variant: :outline, disabled: true) do %> <%= ui_icon("loader-circle", class: "animate-spin") %> Carregando <% end %> Disabled Pass disabled: true as an HTML attribute. Disabled Copy<%= ui_button(disabled: true) { "Disabled" } %> As a link Render as an <a> with tag: :a, keeping the button's look. Go to the dashboard Copy<%= ui_button(tag: :a, href: "#", variant: :outline) { "Go to the dashboard" } %> API reference ui_button(**options, &block) encapsula Ui::ButtonComponent.new(**options). title: Calendar
text: Docs Components Calendar Calendar A month grid built on the client: navigation, single or range selection, and keyboard support. Installation Shadwire follows shadcn/ui's open code model: the component's source is copied into your application and becomes yours. Install it with the CLI: Copyshadwire add calendar --yes The calendar registry item installs these files: app/components/ui_component.rb app/components/ui/calendar_component.rb app/helpers/ui/calendar_helper.rb app/javascript/controllers/ui_calendar_controller.js vendor/shadwire/shadwire.css This component uses Stimulus, so the application needs importmap-rails and stimulus-rails with automatic controller loading. Haven't installed the CLI yet? gem install shadwire, then shadwire init. Usage The server renders only the scaffold; the ui-calendar controller builds the days, so changing month costs no request. The chosen date goes into an input[type=hidden] — the calendar submits like works inside a form_with like any other field. For a field that opens the calendar in a popover, see Date Picker. ExpandCopy<%= ui_calendar(selected: Date.current, name: "date", class: "border") %> <%# Intervalo: duas datas, dois inputs, dois meses. %> <%= ui_calendar( mode: :range, selected: Date.current..(Date.current + 7), number_of_months: 2, name: "trip[starts_on]",<%= ui_calendar(selected: Date.current, name: "date", class: "border") %> <%# Intervalo: duas datas, dois inputs, dois meses. %> <%= ui_calendar( mode: :range, selected: Date.current..(Date.current + 7), number_of_months: 2, name: "trip[starts_on]", end_name: "trip[ends_on]" ) %> Examples Default The current month with today selected. Arrows walk the days, Home/End jump to the ends of the week, and PageUp/PageDown change month. Copy<%# Inline, the calendar draws its own frame; inside a popover the popover plays that part, so the border is left to whoever uses it. %> <%= ui_calendar(selected: Date.today, name: "date", class: "border") %> Range mode: :range records two dates; hovering after the first click previews the range. number_of_months: 2 shows two months side by side. Copy<%= ui_calendar( mode: :range, selected: Date.current..(Date.current + 12), number_of_months: 2, name: "trip[starts_on]", end_name: "trip[ends_on]", class: "border" ) %> Caption with selects caption_layout: :dropdown swaps the month name for month and year selects — the short way to a distant year. Copy<%# `min:`/`max:` desabilitam os dias fora da faixa e delimitam o select de ano. %> <%= ui_calendar( caption_layout: :dropdown, name: "born_on", min: Date.new(1930, 1, 1), max: Date.current, class: "border" ) %> API reference Dates accept a Date or an ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Like every component, it also accepts class / class_name e **attrs. Argument Default Description mode :single :range selects a range; the second click closes the far end. selected — The chosen date. With :range it takes a range (Date..Date). from, to — The ends of the range, when you would rather pass them separately. name, end_name — The hidden inputs. name is the date (or the start); end_name the end. month the selection, otherwise today The first visible month. min, max — Disable the days outside the span, and bound the year select. number_of_months 1 Consecutive months side by side. 2 is the usual pair for ranges. caption_layout :label :dropdown swaps the month name for month and year selects (single month only). year_range −100…+10 anos The years in the select. min:/max: win when given. dir — :rtl mirrors the grid, the navigation arrows and the ←/→ keys. week_start 0 The first day of the week: 0 Sunday, 1 Monday. month_names, day_names pt-BR Caption and header labels, e.g. I18n.t("date.month_names").compact. Events: ui-calendar:change on each selection and ui-calendar:connect when the calendar builds, both carrying detail: { date, from, to }. No sentido inverso, ui-calendar#setDate moves the calendar to a date coming from elsewhere. Previous Button Group Next Card

<%= ui_checkbox(id: "checkbox-terms") %> <%= ui_label(for: "checkbox-terms") { "Accept the terms and conditions" } %>
Checked Use checked: true to render it checked; pair it with supporting text. Receive product news We send at most one email a week. Copy

<%= ui_label(for: "checkbox-newsletter") { "Receive product news" } %>

We send at most one email a week.

Disabled disabled: true disables the native input. Not available on your current plan Copy

<%= ui_checkbox(name: form.field_name(:terms), id: form.field_id(:terms), value: "1") %> <%= ui_label(for: form.field_id(:terms)) { "Li e aceito os termos" } %>
<% end %> API reference ui_checkbox(**options) encapsula Ui::CheckboxComponent.new(**options).
